companyDescription: Launch + lunar + defense · Alpha rocket + Blue Ghost lunar lander + SciTec (space domain awareness) · Q2 2026 revenue up 659% YoY to a record $117.7M, FY26 guidance raised to $420-450M — the real story is fundamentals genuinely improving while the stock has actually given back ground since the pre-earnings pop
priceNote: Prior report (Aug 10) used $26.71 — that price captured a pre-earnings pop (+11.0% same day) heading into the Aug 11 print. The print itself delivered record results (revenue +659% YoY, guidance raised), but the stock has since given back the pre-earnings spike and sits at $23.24, -13.0% vs the Aug 10 report — a 'sell the news'/multiple-compression pattern, not a fundamentals problem. Consensus analyst targets were trimmed alongside (from $40.64 to $38.60) even as guidance went up, which is the clearest evidence this is a valuation reset, not a thesis problem.
summary: Firefly's Q2 2026 print (Aug 11) delivered record revenue of $117.7M, up 659% YoY — a genuine acceleration from Q1's 45% YoY pace — with FY26 guidance raised to $420-450M (80%+ pre-booked via backlog). New contract wins have kept landing since: an SSC Space multi-launch deal (Alpha from Sweden, 2028+), a NASA Spacecraft Processing Operations Contract at Vandenberg, SciTec's $93.7M Space Force radar-digitization contract, a Lockheed Martin contract extension, and a new ISO Class 8 cleanroom (completed Sep 22) that can assemble up to 12 Blue Ghost/Elytra vehicles simultaneously. Despite all this, the stock is DOWN -13.0% versus the Aug 10 report's pre-earnings price, and the 10-analyst consensus target fell to $38.60 from $40.64 — the market priced in the good news early and is now digesting execution risk on the steep H2 ramp the guidance implies. Alpha's full Block II configuration (Flight 8) still has not flown as of late Sep 2026, slipping past its 'late summer 2026' guided window with no new confirmed date — the real de-risking event for the core launch business remains outstanding.

catalysts.name: Q3 2026 Earnings
catalysts.description: Reports Nov 11, 2026. Tests whether the raised FY26 guidance ($420-450M revenue) holds after Q2's 659% YoY beat — the H2 ramp implied by that guidance is a real execution test, not a formality. Market will also want an update on SSC Space, NASA, and Space Force contract cadence, plus any Alpha Flight 8 timeline.

catalysts.name: Alpha Block II Debut (Flight 8) — Overdue
catalysts.description: Still hasn't flown as of late Sep 2026, having slipped past the 'late summer 2026' guided window with no new confirmed date. Flight 7 (Mar 2026) already validated key Block II sub-components and popped the stock +12.77%; the FULL configuration debut on Flight 8 remains the true de-risking event for the launch business.

risks: Alpha Flight 8 (full Block II configuration) has slipped past its own 'late summer 2026' guided window with no new confirmed date as of late Sep 2026 — a real, live schedule risk that the Aug 10 report expected to be resolved by now
FY26 guidance of $420-450M implies a steep H2 ramp from the $117.7M Q2 print — Nov 11 earnings is a genuine test of execution, not just a formality

The stock's -13.0% drift since the Aug 10 report despite record Q2 results, alongside a $40.64→$38.60 consensus-target trim, shows the market pricing in real execution skepticism, not just profit-taking
Net loss was $92.3M in Q2 despite the revenue beat — still cash-burning at scale even as growth accelerates
Heavy dilution history: shares outstanding grew significantly post-IPO and post-SciTec — further issuance risk remains live
Extreme realized volatility even on good news — the stock has swung double digits in both directions repeatedly through 2026

macroRisk.rateOutlook: Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16, 2026 (first hike since 2023); next FOMC Oct 27-28, 2026 — well before Nov 11 earnings. Rising Treasury yields have been an active headwind for high-multiple, cash-burning growth names this quarter.
macroRisk.inflationNote: Core inflation remains above target — a persistent headwind for space-sector capex-heavy names generally.
macroRisk.sectorImpact: The space sector's sentiment has stabilized somewhat as Firefly's own fundamentals caught up to the news flow, but the sector remains sensitive to broad risk-off moves and capital rotation (e.g. toward SpaceX's IPO).
macroRisk.summary: MEDIUM — Firefly's contract wins are macro-independent, but the stock's post-earnings pullback shows it's still exposed to broad growth-stock rate sensitivity and execution skepticism, same as its space-sector peers.

entryStrategy.verdict: SPECULATIVE — measured median at-catalyst return across the core lane is -6.9% (n=54); buying at today's $23.24 is not the default entry. Prefer the $19.50-21.00 dip zone ahead of Nov 11 earnings. This is a genuine fundamentals story (659% YoY revenue growth, raised guidance, real contract wins) trading against a market that already front-ran the good news and is now pricing execution risk on the H2 ramp — the gap between story and price has actually widened since the last report, not closed.
